newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FCL Paper sees mixed 2nd half.
newsitem.headline: FCL Paper sees mixed 2nd half.

text.p: - Fletcher Challenge Paper said on Wednesday it faced a mixed outlook for the remainder of the fiscal year to June 1997.
The company also commented that the stronger U.S. dollar may serve to delay pulp price increases and that current pulp inventories were too high to support such increases.
Improving market fundamentals -- lower inventory and higher demand -- had led to the announcement of an increase for newsprint prices in North America, effective 1997.
Other publication paper markets, and the fine paper market, were exhibiting better demand than was seen in the first half of the current fiscal year, FCL Paper said.
"However, there is less certainty about about improvement in prices in the near term," the division said.
"In pulp markets, continuing high inventories will affect the ability of producers to implement price increases in the immediate future," it said.
"The recent strengthening of the U.S. dollar against other major world currencies may also serve to delay price increases for key global markets," it said.
FCL Paper earlier announced a net loss of NZ$40 million for the half year to December, against a profit of $186 million for the corresponding year-ago period.

Operating earnings included a payment of NZ$30 million received from the New Zealand government as consideration for Fletcher Challenge releasing the Crown from an indemnity in respect of fibre supply to the Kawerau mill.
Also included was the one-time cost of the Fletcher Challenge Canada restructuring, of C$25 million (NZ$26 million), which would result in ongoing savings in the order of C$25-30 million.
